# GT8-10 operator control research, 2026-10-24

Scope: read-only primary-source check of `docs/designs/governed-command-tools.md` GT-C5 and `docs/designs/command-governance.md` CG-13/14. No native prompt, installation, credential access, or repo edit. Consequences below are recommendations/inferences from cited APIs, not a claim that a host is qualified.

## Conclusions for the receiver

1. **Authenticate sources, then compose.** A path named `organization` does not establish an organization issuer. Keep protected trust anchors and a registered source roster outside candidate write access; require exact issuer/key, subject/target, schema/version, content hash, policy epoch, sequence, expiry and revocation freshness for each required layer before using it. Persist the highest accepted epoch/version and refuse older or mixed snapshots. TUF illustrates separate root/delegated roles, hash-bound consistent snapshots, version and expiration checks, while explicitly addressing rollback and freeze attacks. This is a design analogy, **not** a proposal to implement TUF. [TUF roles](https://theupdateframework.io/docs/metadata/), [TUF security](https://theupdateframework.io/docs/security/). Confidence: high for the failure modes; medium for exact receiver record fields pending implementation design.

2. **Use an exact, finite maintenance grant.** The trusted receiver should issue a nonce and show a canonical plan containing action, advisory control IDs, permitted old/new values, exact candidate bytes/digest, host/project/principal, issuer and approver, policy/config hashes and epoch, deadline, maximum duration, reason/ticket, and rollback target. Sign or otherwise issuer-authenticate that exact record. Verify nonce unused; snapshot/epoch current; requested diff a subset of the grant; independent mandatory floors unchanged; no concurrent lease expansion. Consume the nonce durably with the transition, then atomically promote only evaluated bytes. Revocation must be checked at every protected operation, not by a one-shot approval or timer. This is the direct consequence of GT-C5/CG-14 and TUF's anti-replay/freshness pattern. Confidence: high for controls, medium for storage mechanics.

3. **Clock and crash are receiver obligations.** Persist lease ID, policy epoch, expiry, consumed nonce and transition journal outside candidate writes. On process restart, reload trusted floors and journal before accepting operations. Use elapsed monotonic time for a running lease, plus a persisted wall-clock floor/high-watermark and a trusted time source or explicit hold after reboot if time cannot be established. Any backward jump, stale revocation view, journal gap, ambiguous promote/rollback, or expired lease holds advisory change; mandatory controls stay armed. A monotonic clock alone does not survive reboot, and a signed expiry does not make wall time trustworthy. TUF expiration detects freeze only when client time is usable. [TUF metadata](https://theupdateframework.io/docs/metadata/). Confidence: high design inference; native durability requires qualification.

## Native presence and authority

| Platform | Primary facts | GT consequence |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `LAContext.evaluatePolicy` establishes successful evaluation of a chosen local authentication policy; `deviceOwnerAuthentication` can use Touch ID, Apple Watch or user password on macOS. `canEvaluatePolicy` is only an availability check and may change. Keychain `SecAccessControl.userPresence` gates access to an item; a protected private key can sign bytes via `SecKeyCreateSignature`. Authentication reuse can be configured; default Touch ID reuse duration is zero. [LAContext](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/localauthentication/lacontext), [policy](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/LocalAuthentication/LAPolicy/deviceOwnerAuthentication), [Keychain](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/localauthentication/accessing-keychain-items-with-face-id-or-touch-id), [signature](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/seckeycreatesignature%28_%3A_%3A_%3A_%3A%29), [reuse](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/LocalAuthentication/LAContext/touchIDAuthenticationAllowableReuseDuration) | A Boolean LA success is not an exact grant. Prefer a protected key operation over the receiver's nonce+plan digest, verify with an enrolled public key mapped to an authorized approver, and prevent context reuse where each approval requires a fresh gesture. Keychain presence alone does not supply organization role or candidate diff authority. Authorization Services is a separate OS rights route, not a substitute for the plan binding. [Authorization Services](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Security/authorization-services) |
| Windows | `UserConsentVerifier` verifies the logged-on user through a configured device, but yields a result enum only. Desktop use is `IUserConsentVerifierInterop::RequestVerificationForWindowAsync` with an HWND. `KeyCredential.RequestSignAsync` signs caller data with a Hello credential after user verification; Microsoft describes challenge response and warns to design replay prevention. Hardware attestation is optional and software fallback exists. [consent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.security.credentials.ui.userconsentverifier), [desktop interop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/userconsentverifierinterop/nf-userconsentverifierinterop-iuserconsentverifierinterop-requestverificationforwindowasync), [Hello](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/security/windows-hello), [sign](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.security.credentials.keycredential.requestsignasync) | `Verified` alone proves local verification, not approver authority or exact plan consent. Prefer receiver-issued challenge with plan digest, registered key and verified signature. Record whether TPM-backed assurance is actually required and observed; never infer it from Hello availability. Qualify desktop API/version and account/key binding natively. |
| Linux | polkit `CheckAuthorization` checks a subject and action ID, can prompt on a user-triggered request, and returns authorized/challenge. Subject can use pidfd+uid or PID/start-time/uid; `pkcheck` warns of process identification races. Details need a sufficiently privileged checker. polkit has retained temporary authorizations and revocation APIs. PAM provides service-configurable authentication, not a built-in exact action grant. [authority](https://polkit.pages.freedesktop.org/polkit/eggdbus-interface-org.freedesktop.PolicyKit1.Authority.html), [pkcheck](https://polkit.pages.freedesktop.org/polkit/pkcheck.1.html), [PAM](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/pam.8.html) | Use an installed, deployment-owned polkit action/policy for the specific receiver, from a protected process, with subject identity pinned; disable retained broad auth for per-plan approval. If PAM is selected, pair successful authentication with separately protected issuer/role and exact plan authorization. Neither PAM success nor polkit `is_authorized` proves that candidate bytes match the maintenance grant. |

Native result is only one conjunct: user presence/OS action, enrolled identity and role, fresh exact grant, candidate equality, independent floors, receiver control. Failure or unavailable adapter holds a change that requires it. Do not solicit/store passwords in Go or synthesize biometric success.

## Reuse boundaries

TUF is useful for trusted-role, snapshot, expiry and rollback concepts; in-toto binds authorized functionaries to layout steps and signed link metadata, not local hook authority ([in-toto](https://in-toto.io/docs/getting-started/)). Sigstore verifies artifact signature **and** certificate identity/issuer, with optional transparency evidence, but that does not establish active lease or local host control ([Sigstore verify](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/verifying/verify/)). OPA bundle signatures are enforced only when signing verification is configured; keys alone can allow unsigned bundles ([OPA bundles](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-bundles)). Cedar returns an authorization answer for supplied principal/action/resource/context, but a policy error is skipped unless the caller inspects diagnostics; this is incompatible with silently lowering a mandatory floor ([Cedar authorization](https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html)). Reuse existing narrow Policy Kit/guard contracts and stdlib crypto for exact receipts. Do not embed a universal policy, signing, update or provenance engine in the Go command.

## Proof split and rejected shortcuts

Hermetic: canonical encoding and signature verification, wrong issuer/role/target/field, exact-delta subset, replay/concurrent leases, stale/revoked/future epochs, wall-clock rollback, expiry, journal crash points, candidate mismatch, independent negative probes, mandatory floor preservation, atomic state-machine transitions using injected clock/storage faults. Native qualification: real macOS/Windows/Linux prompt and key behavior, approver enrollment/role mapping, protected storage and process boundary, OS policy setup, hook interception and per-operation revocation/expiry after process crash or reboot. Build/cross-compile is neither installation nor native qualification.

Reject: global bypass flag; candidate-writable trust root; cached `allow` or auth Boolean; biometric/Hello/PAM/polkit success treated as policy grant; arbitrary tuning during a time window; expiry enforced only by wakeup; extended lease after clock rollback; signed but stale config; optional unsigned policy accepted because a key exists; treating Cedar `Allow` with skipped errors as full mandatory safety; treating uninstalled code as intercepted host events. Same-user control that can replace the dispatcher/trust root remains outside this boundary; file location alone cannot establish protection.

## HC-2 DSSE protocol followup, 2026-10-24

Upstream [DSSE protocol v1.0.2](https://github.com/secure-systems-lab/dsse/blob/master/protocol.md) defines the signature over `PAE(UTF8(payloadType), serializedBody)`. PAE is the exact byte sequence `"DSSEv1" || 0x20 || decimal byte length of UTF-8 type without leading zeroes || 0x20 || UTF-8 type || 0x20 || decimal payload byte length without leading zeroes || 0x20 || raw payload`. Lengths count **bytes**, not characters or base64 text. The [JSON envelope](https://github.com/secure-systems-lab/dsse/blob/master/envelope.md) has `payloadType`, base64 `payload`, and `signatures` with base64 `sig` and optional `keyid`. `keyid` is expressly an **unauthenticated hint**, never a trust decision. DSSE leaves the signature algorithm and trust/key management out of band; fixed Ed25519 over PAE with an independently enrolled, nonrevoked key is a valid application choice. Verify the exact decoded payload bytes and pass those same bytes to parsing.

**HC-2 disposition:** The initial draft's PAE expression and raw-payload hash were correct. Research rejected its mandatory key hint and padded-standard-base64-only restriction: the selected profile now accepts canonical standard or URL-safe base64, padded or unpadded, and ignores optional `keyid` for trust. The expected independently enrolled key alone selects verification authority. Exactly one signature and closed envelope fields remain explicit application restrictions. Upstream permits multisig and extension fields, so this is a deliberately restricted DSSE wire profile, not a general DSSE verifier. Confidence: high from upstream protocol/envelope; the research itself did not test implementation or native behavior. Independent interoperability fixtures must prove the implemented subset.
